guide.summary: The Pyramids of Giza, Saqqara, Al-Moez Street and the National Museum of Egyptian Civilization, with hotel restaurants, cafés, bakeries and bars checked against their own websites.
guide.tip: The ministry asks you to arrive at least an hour before closing, and last entry at the Pyramids of Giza and Saqqara is 4:00 pm, so start at the Pyramids when they open at 7:00 am.

toolkit.label: Closing days
toolkit.copy: The ministry portal lists the Pyramids of Giza and Saqqara as open on all days, with shorter Ramadan hours. The National Museum of Egyptian Civilization opens Saturday to Thursday from 9:00 am to 5:00 pm and adds a Friday evening session from 6:00 pm to 9:00 pm.

toolkit.label: Tickets
toolkit.copy: The Pyramids of Giza, Saqqara and Al-Moez Street sell dated tickets through the ministry portal, where the Pyramids list EGP 700 for foreign adults. The National Museum of Egyptian Civilization sells its last daytime ticket at 4:00 pm.

toolkit.label: Walk-ins
toolkit.copy: Kempinski Nile Hotel says walk-ins are welcome subject to seating, but advance booking is recommended for dinner at venues such as Osmanly. Khufu's takes reservations separately for breakfast and lunch and for dinner.

toolkit.label: Rules
toolkit.copy: At the Pyramids of Giza and Saqqara the ministry asks you to arrive at least an hour before closing. The Rooftop, The Jazz Bar and Osmanly at the Kempinski Nile Hotel list a smart casual dress code.

guide.dek: Do the Pyramids of Giza at opening, keep a Friday evening for the National Museum of Egyptian Civilization, and eat in Zamalek, Garden City or on the Corniche.
intro: The Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities runs Cairo's ancient sites, and its ticket portal lists the Pyramids of Giza as open every day from 7:00 am, with last entry at 4:00 pm and adult tickets for foreign visitors at EGP 700. The ministry asks you to arrive at least an hour before a site closes, so an early start pays off. Saqqara follows a similar pattern, opening daily at 8:00 am with last entry at 4:00 pm, and both sites have shorter hours during Ramadan.

In the city, the National Museum of Egyptian Civilization on Al-Fustat Road, home to the Royal Mummies Gallery, opens Saturday to Thursday from 9:00 am to 5:00 pm, with its last ticket sold at 4:00 pm. On Fridays it adds an evening session from 6:00 pm to 9:00 pm, a useful slot if your days are full. Al-Moez Street, the ticketed historic street in Islamic Cairo, opens daily from 9:00 am with last entry at 4:00 pm.

Near the pyramids, 139 Pavilion at Marriott Mena House, 6 Pyramids Road, is open 24 hours, serving buffet breakfast, lunch and dinner with live music, and hosts a Saturday brunch from 1:00 to 4:00 pm. Alfredo, the hotel's Italian restaurant, opens daily from 4:00 pm to 11:00 pm. Khufu's sits inside the archaeological grounds, reached through the visitor entrance, and takes reservations for breakfast and lunch and for dinner.

In Zamalek, the Cairo Marriott at 16 Saray El Gezira Street lists the Garden Promenade Cafe from 6:00 am to 2:00 am, The Bakery around the clock and Harry's Pub from 6:00 pm to 1:00 am. At the Kempinski Nile Hotel in Garden City, The Rooftop serves from 9:00 am to 2:00 am and Osmanly from 1:00 pm to midnight, both with a smart casual dress code. On the Corniche, the St. Regis lists J&G Steakhouse from 4:30 pm to midnight.
summaryCards: Start at the Pyramids of Giza when they open at 7:00 am, then lunch at 139 Pavilion at Marriott Mena House, which is open 24 hours.
Have breakfast at the Garden Promenade Cafe in Zamalek, open from 6:00 am, before an unhurried visit to the National Museum of Egyptian Civilization.
Book the Pyramids of Giza and Saqqara on the ministry's egymonuments.com portal, and reserve dinner ahead at Kempinski Nile Hotel venues such as Osmanly.

limitations: Website review, not a visit or telephone confirmation. Advertised opening, booking and exhibition details do not guarantee availability. Only 21 places met the address rule, below the 25-35 target. Ten major sights, including the Grand Egyptian Museum, the Egyptian Museum, the Citadel and the Cairo Opera House, were left out because their official pages publish no address or location, not because of any closure. The Pyramids of Giza, Saqqara and Al-Moez Street are confirmed by site name only, the ministry's seasonal date ranges appear only in images, Kempinski Nile Hotel pages give only "Garden City Cairo", and Khufu's publishes no opening hours. Several candidates could not be read: gem.eg, egyptianmuseumcairo.eg, Four Seasons, Diwan and Espresso Lab returned 403; Al-Azhar Park and Felfela had SSL errors; Abou El Sid, Cairo Jazz Club and Cairo Tower returned no readable content; the Nile Ritz-Carlton returned 404 and Marriott pages were then rate-limited.
